newsitem.title: KUWAIT: U.S. troops end Kuwait crisis pullout in mid-month.
newsitem.headline: U.S. troops end Kuwait crisis pullout in mid-month.

text.p: U.S. troops deployed in Kuwait during Washington's September standoff with Baghdad will complete their pullout from the Gulf Arab state in mid-December, a U.S. embassy spokeswoman said on Monday.
"They have started to leave," said the spokeswoman. Their multi-stage departure will last "until about December 15."

Former U.S. Defence Secretary William Perry said in November the United States had decided to remove 4,200 American troops from Kuwait by Christmas but would maintain 1,800 Marines aboard ships off-shore.
The soldiers took part in Washington's troop buildup in the Gulf during a standoff between the United States and Iraq over attacks by Baghdad's forces against Kurds in northern Iraq in August.
The Iraqi move prompted the United States to launch two waves of missile strikes in southern Iraq in September.
Some 3,000 troops were flown to Kuwait from the 1st Cavalry Division in Fort Hood, Texas in September to join some 1,200 soldiers who were taking part in a military exercise in Kuwait.
Perry, in a visit to Kuwait last month, said Washington had decided to keep eight Stealth fighters in Kuwait as a warning message to Iraqi President Saddam Hussein not to invade Kuwait again.

A U.S.-led military coalition drove Iraqi troops from Kuwait in the 1991 Gulf War. Since the war the United States kept pre-positioned weapons, including main battle tanks, in Kuwait to be used by U.S. troops to deter any Iraqi aggression.
